propositions: The LLM judge exhibits self-consistency drift when re-running Pass-2/Pass-3 decisions on the same findings; this noise injects instability into Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary that R5 depends on.
Section-order permutation of input plans can flip gate verdicts (order sensitivity); residual order-sensitivity must be measured empirically before R3 lands a new order-exposed container criterion.
Exp A measures self-consistency over 50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort (the R5 routing set) by collecting 3 votes per finding and computing Fleiss' κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8 as the pass floor.

Exp B measures verdict stability under section-order shuffle over 14 plans with ≥3 top-level sections using 3 distinct deterministic permutations (identity + 2 seeded), applying the same κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8 floor.

Infra-INDETERMINATE verdicts carrying coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed are execution failures, not stable judge outcomes, and are dropped-and-re-run; genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (no flag) is kept as an agreement category.

E6 is a measurement-only experiment that re-judges existing samples to compare repeated judge outputs to each other (not against gold truth), gating R5 on self-consistency pass and R3 on order-shuffle pass.
